ns0:entry.ns0:title: feat(datasets): disk-less episode-pool video streaming (#3917)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(datasets): disk-less episode-pool video streaming (#3917)

* Add episode video streaming byte cache

* Pin Hub range cache and datasets main sources

* Make episode cache benchmark fetch-only by default

* Retry transient native HTTP range failures

* Use full MP4 sidecar for episode cache benchmark

* Report full dataset estimate in episode cache benchmark

* Report episode cache fill stage timings

* Add random frame range fetch benchmark

* Report memory usage in cache benchmarks

* Use HfFileSystem for sidecar episode benchmark

* Remove random frame benchmark path

* Report range read timing breakdown

* Allow native HTTP sidecar range diagnostics

* Tune native HTTP range diagnostics

* Log episode cache fill progress

* Report native HTTP chunk timing

* Allow dynamic range timing counters

* Track native HTTP failed attempt timing

* Retry native HTTP timeout statuses

* Clarify native HTTP exception timing

* Instrument HfFileSystem range requests

* Log failed HTTP range attempts

* Add GOP window range benchmark

* Benchmark random sampling from episode pool

* Fix pool sampling camera timestamps

* Add distributed episode pool benchmark summaries

* Fix episode pool stream benchmark pacing

* perf(streaming): sub-range parallel fetch + non-blocking pool replacement

The 64-vs-128-worker benchmark pair proved a per-host throughput ceiling
(~270 MiB/s) on the HF bucket path: doubling connections exactly halved
per-connection speed (4.8 -> 2.2 MiB/s) and left the aggregate flat,
while per-episode latency doubled (5.7s -> 12s) and keep-up worsened.
Steady-state demand (148 MiB/s) is well below the ceiling; the keep-up
misses come entirely from consumer stalls (refill_wait 14-19s of ~84s):
the sim blocks the training hot path on ensure_ready() for the FIFO-head
replacement while episodes take 5.7-12s to arrive.

Two fixes:

- Non-blocking replacements: EpisodeByteCache.is_ready() (all cameras
  cached or futures done, no blocking) and the stream sim now swaps a
  replacement only when it is already resident, deferring otherwise;
  fetch capacity (~2x demand) repays the debt on later batches. A
  deferred_swaps metric is reported.
- Sub-range parallel fetch (native-http): --range-subranges N splits one
  camera GET into N concurrent sub-range GETs. Under a per-host ceiling
  this adds no bandwidth but divides per-episode latency by ~N. Keep
  workers x subranges near the ~64-connection saturation point (e.g.
  --workers 16 --range-subranges 4).

Verified: sub-range span math + order-preserving concat and is_ready
semantics (unit-level, network stubbed).

* feat(streaming): exact-once epoch coverage for the byte-cache episode pool

The pool path sampled frames with replacement and never guaranteed a full
epoch (episodes rotated on a fixed cadence; frames drawn randomly, none
tracked). Add ExactCoveragePool: a deterministic planner that enumerates
every frame of every episode exactly once per epoch while keeping at most
pool_size episodes resident, so batch mixing stays high (uniform draw over
all remaining frames in the pool) but coverage is complete and reproducible.

Mechanics (the "evict only when all frames sampled" model): episodes are
admitted in a seeded global permutation; each resident episode carries a
seeded frame-index shuffle; each draw picks a resident episode with
probability proportional to its remaining frames and pops one; an episode
is evicted only when its last frame is emitted, then a new one is admitted;
the epoch ends when admission is exhausted and every resident episode drains.
Order is a pure function of (seed, epoch) -> resumable by deterministic
fast-forward. The planner does no I/O and exposes admission_order so callers
can prefetch episodes ahead of the sampling frontier.

Wired into the benchmark as --coverage {sampled,exact}: run_exact_coverage_stream
prefetches stream_prefetch_episodes beyond the frontier so a freshly admitted
episode's bytes are resident before it is drawn, then decodes each frame once,
paced to target.

Tests: 7 planner unit tests (exact-once coverage incl. a 45k-frame epoch,
pool-size bound, per-(seed,epoch) determinism with coverage preserved,
admission/eviction events, coupon-collector mixing, zero-length episodes) and
a mocked-cache structural test of run_exact_coverage_stream asserting
every-frame-once-per-camera plus the prefetch-before-decode invariant.

* refactor(streaming): exact coverage is the only pool mode

Drop the with-replacement sampled path: delete run_pool_stream_simulation
and the --coverage flag; the streaming keep-up sim always uses
run_exact_coverage_stream (ExactCoveragePool), so every frame of every
episode is decoded exactly once per epoch. --pool-samples-per-episode is
kept as a deprecated no-op so existing commands still parse (exact mode
evicts an episode only when all its frames are emitted, so a turnover
cadence no longer applies).

* feat(dataset): integrate episode streaming into training

* refactor(dataset): make streaming pool rank-owned

* refactor(streaming): split episode data plane

* chore(streaming): remove obsolete benchmark flags

* Fix streaming Parquet imports and video fallback

* Preserve private Hub auth in streaming readers

* Harden production dataset streaming pipeline

* Derive streaming decoder cap from episode pool

* Remove streaming benchmark prototypes

* feat(datasets): write videos with faststart for seekable playback

Pass movflags=faststart when opening MP4 outputs so the moov atom is
placed at the front of the file. Decoders can then seek without reading
the whole file, which speeds up random-access frame decoding.

* refactor(datasets): batch DatasetReader access in get_items

Make _query_hf_dataset, _get_query_timestamps and _query_videos
batch-aware (list-of-items) so get_items gathers tabular rows in a
single Arrow read and groups video decoding by physical MP4 file across
the whole batch. Update the Groot caller for the new signature and add a
batched-vs-single equivalence test.

* perf(datasets): drop nearest-match re-stack in torchcodec decode

get_frames_at returns exactly one frame per requested index, in order,
so frame i already corresponds to timestamps[i]. Index the batch
directly and compare timestamps elementwise instead of running a cdist
nearest-match and re-stacking the frames — that redundant copy dominated
decode overhead.

* perf(datasets): pin one row group per episode for large episodes

Pass row_group_size >= episode length so episodes exceeding PyArrow's
default 1Mi-row split threshold still map to exactly one row group,
preserving episode<->row-group alignment.

* chore(format): formatting code

* docs(streaming): document public primitives

* fix(streaming): preserve video timing and bound episode payloads

* perf(streaming): project columns before temporal reads

* perf(streaming): share mapped indexes and prune parquet row groups

* feat(streaming): Add opt-in shuffled round-robin sampling

Preserve remaining-frame weighting by default and expose round-robin through the training config. Reuse byte-aware admission and frame coverage while deferring new residents until the next round.

Cover deterministic replay, byte leases, temporal and RGB parity, factory wiring, rank sharding and worker resume. Document finite-prefix mixing and throughput trade-offs.

* fix(streaming): stabilize regression tests and preserve map-style decoding

* fix(streaming): Harden lifecycle and resume contracts

Pin source identities, bound resource lifetimes, and preserve deterministic resume. Simplify bucket configuration and document typed streaming interfaces. Regenerate lockfile markers without upgrading dependencies.

* fix(streaming): Identify index generations from open files

* perf(streaming): Read sidecar arrays by archive member

* perf(streaming): Retain validated indexes during sidecar install

* perf(streaming): Bound parallel sidecar decompression

* perf(streaming): Prepare numeric episode columns once

* perf(streaming): Keep startup index reads file-local

Project metadata once, combine span and admission-size preparation, and count mini-MP4 bytes without serializing per-sample tables. Preserve planner order and exact compressed-byte accounting.

* test(streaming): Guard optional dataset imports before collection

* fix(streaming): Protect concurrent ZIP header reads

Hold the ZIP reader's source lock across member opening on older Python versions. Keep array decompression outside the lock and verify parallel output parity and cleanup.

* fix(streaming): Refresh expired signed URLs on unauthorized reads

* fix(streaming): Address final review findings and remove legacy helpers

* fix(batch decoding): removing batch video decoding to avoid competition with the mutliple DataLoader workers

* perf(streaming): cache per-episode metadata and check PTS tolerance with floats

Read dataset_from_index and each camera's from_timestamp once when an
episode joins the pool instead of formatting a full meta.episodes row
(including every stats column) twice per sample. Compare decoded PTS
against query timestamps with plain floats instead of building small
torch tensors per camera. Same rule (abs(query - decoded) <= tolerance_s,
NaN still fails), byte-identical output, less GIL time per sample.

Co-authored-by: Hadrien Cornier <29749923+Hadrien-Cornier@users.noreply.github.com>
Signed-off-by: Pepijn <pepijn@huggingface.co>

* refactor(streaming): address review feedback on config, validation and docs

- Accept an hf://buckets/OWNER/BUCKET root in StreamingLeRobotDataset and
  the streaming factory path (is_bucket_root in storage.py), mirroring how
  LeRobotDataset derives that URI from repo_type="bucket".
- Replace the sampling-strategy string literals with a
  StreamingSamplingStrategy str-enum.
- Reuse the video_decoder_cache_size name (LeRobotDataset) instead of
  streaming_max_open_decoders, and expose it on DatasetConfig.
- Drop duplicated argument validation from StreamingLeRobotDataset and
  EpisodeByteCache; DatasetConfig stays the single CLI validation point.
- Select episodes with resolve_episode_indices.
- Rename streaming/_mapped_index.py to streaming/sidecar_utils.py.
- Docs: shorten the dataset-v3 streaming section and link to the streaming
  page; explain workers, shards and in-process concurrency; add
  max_num_shards to the options table; troubleshooting as a table.

* refactor(datasets): share one root parser between storage and streaming

Add StorageLocation (lerobot/streaming/location.py) to classify dataset
roots once: local path, hf://datasets, hf://buckets, other hf:// URIs
and generic fsspec URLs, with the repo id, revision, in-repo path,
pinned commit, Hub storage options and byte-range backend. It stays free
of the datasets extra so the streaming primitives can use it, and
storage.py re-exports it with dataset_location(), is_remote_uri() and
is_bucket_root() built on top.

This replaces the hand-written bucket splitting in range_fetch and
streaming_sidecar, the three copies of the pinned-commit regex, the
three token-to-storage-options copies, range_backend_for_root and
_pin_hub_root, and the hf:// URI builders in dataset metadata,
LeRobotDataset and the Lance backend. Data roots, published sidecar
URLs and sidecar cache keys are unchanged.

* perf(streaming): read MP4 sidecar headers with exact-size probes

Start indexing each source MP4 with a 512 KiB read instead of 4 MiB.
A truncated box header gives its exact size, so the next read fetches
only the rest of that box instead of doubling from byte 0, and when the
media payload comes first the movie box is read from the file tail
straight away. The parsed index is unchanged; sidecar builds read far
fewer bytes, especially for datasets that store moov after mdat.

Co-authored-by: Hadrien Cornier <29749923+Hadrien-Cornier@users.noreply.github.com>
Signed-off-by: Pepijn <pepijn@huggingface.co>

* perf(streaming): apply image transforms on the decode threads

Augmentations ran on the loader's main thread after each decode, which
made them the serial bottleneck when image transforms are enabled. Run
them inside the decode task instead so they parallelize with decoding.

RandomSubsetApply now iterates a local copy of its selection, so
concurrent calls from different decode threads cannot apply each
other's subset. Because draws from the global torch RNG now interleave
across threads, a fixed seed no longer reproduces the same random
augmentations; the docs say so.

Co-authored-by: Hadrien Cornier <29749923+Hadrien-Cornier@users.noreply.github.com>
Signed-off-by: Pepijn <pepijn@huggingface.co>

* refactor(streaming): drop debug instrumentation and dead cache helpers

- Remove the timing counters and timing_summary() from both range
  fetchers and EpisodeByteCache, and the LEROBOT_HTTP_FAILURE_LOG
  JSONL failure log with its request-id header. Retries, backoff and
  signed-URL refresh behave exactly as before.
- Remove EpisodeByteCache.ensure_ready/is_ready/get_decoder and the
  open_decoders flag; production decodes through get_frames only.
- Drop the per-row episode check in EpisodeParquetReader, already
  guaranteed by the episode filter just before it.
- Drop __all__ from storage.py; callers import the location helpers
  from lerobot.streaming.location directly.

* refactor(datasets): share item-assembly helpers between map-style and streaming

Move the code both DatasetReader and StreamingLeRobotDataset duplicated
into shared helpers, so both readers assemble items the same way:

- datasets/utils.py: delta_window (clamped window + padding mask, for
  absolute or episode-local rows), shift_timestamps and task_name.
- video_utils.py: depth_encoder_configs, image_depth_units,
  dequantize_depth_frames, convert_image_depth_units,
  normalize_rgb_frames (also used by both video decoders) and
  apply_rgb_transforms.

Delta validation stays in feature_utils (check_delta_timestamps /
get_delta_indices), which both readers already share. Outputs are
unchanged for map-style and streaming loading.

Deprecate the no-op StreamingLeRobotDataset(streaming=...) argument: it
now warns, and streaming is chosen through dataset.streaming instead.

* fix(streaming): key mapped sidecar indexes on archive checksums too

The derived memory-mapped index was keyed only on the sidecar's
(dev, inode, size, mtime_ns, ctime_ns). On Linux, file timestamps move
in coarse ticks and a rewritten file can reuse the freed inode, so a
same-size sidecar replaced within a few milliseconds got the old key
and was served the previous generation's index. That is what made
test_sidecar_payload_does_not_reuse_stale_path_generation fail on the
GPU CI container while passing on macOS.

Add a digest of the ZIP central directory (member names, sizes and
CRC-32s) to the key. It is read once from the opened descriptor, never
decompressing arrays; mid-conversion checks still compare stat identity
because workers share that descriptor. A new test reproduces the
repeated-identity case on any filesystem.

* perf(streaming): assemble items with NumPy and open decoders on bytes

Under the GIL, the small torch ops in item assembly (indexing, clone,
item) release the GIL and wait to take it back behind the decode
threads. Following Hadrien's profiling on PR 3917:

- Keep each resident episode's numeric columns as NumPy arrays and wrap
  copied rows/windows with torch.from_numpy; read task names from a
  list built once, and run the episode/index checks on the arrays.
- Make the shared delta_window NumPy-based, so map-style and streaming
  keep one clamping and padding rule.
- Hand TorchCodec the raw bytes, so FFmpeg reads memory directly instead
  of through a Python read callback that needs the GIL.

Outputs are unchanged. On lerobot/svla_so101_pickplace (Apple M-series,
decode_threads=2, 5 paired runs each) the streamed samples are
byte-identical and throughput rises by a median 6.5% per item and 5%
through a 1-worker DataLoader with batch 8; Hadrien measured 1.30x on
8-vCPU EPYC machines with AV1 data.

Co-Authored-By: Hadrien Cornier <29749923+Hadrien-Cornier@users.noreply.github.com>
Signed-off-by: Pepijn <pepijn@huggingface.co>

ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(flow-matching): share training-input construction across policies (#4631)

* feat(flow-matching): share training-input construction across policies

Inference-time integration and sampling are shared, but every policy still
hand-rolled the training-time noising. Promote pi05's private
`_build_flow_matching_inputs` into `common/flow_matching` as
`make_flow_matching_inputs`, generalized over `FlowConvention`.

The helper centralizes the three things the convention decides: the
interpolation, the sign of the velocity target, and the time given to clean
prefix tokens.

- NOISE_AT_ONE: x_t = t * noise + (1 - t) * actions, v = noise - actions
- NOISE_AT_ZERO: x_t = (1 - t) * noise + t * actions, v = actions - noise

`prefix_mask` gives clean action-prefix positions the model time at the clean
end of the schedule, which makes the interpolation itself return the clean
action there. This is the training-time counterpart of `euler_integrate`'s
`hard_prefix`/`hard_prefix_mask`.

Training and inference stay consistent as long as a policy hands both halves
the same convention. That remains the caller's responsibility: the convention
is an argument to each function, not a property of the policy, and nothing
here rejects a pair that disagrees.

Adopted for training-time noising by all seven flow-matching policies: pi0,
pi05, smolvla, eo1, groot, wall_x and evo1. Each call site is pinned
bit-identical against a verbatim copy of the expression it replaces.

Two things deliberately stay with each policy:

- Loss masking and reduction, including pi05's `_reduce_training_rtc_loss`,
  since their semantics differ.
- evo1's velocity target. It takes the shared interpolation but still builds
  `actions.float() - noise.float()` locally, because it regresses in fp32
  outside its autocast block; the bf16 difference the helper returns is a
  different number. Sharing that too would need a precision-aware target
  helper, which is out of scope here.

ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(flow-matching): explicit flow convention for the shared Euler solver (groot, evo1, wall_x) (#4075)

* feat(flow-matching): give the shared solver an explicit flow convention

euler_integrate only described the openpi schedule (noise at t=1). Name the
convention explicitly and migrate the forward-convention policies onto it:

- add FlowConvention.NOISE_AT_ONE (default, unchanged for pi0/pi05/smolvla/
  eo1) and NOISE_AT_ZERO for groot/evo1/wall_x
- convert to RTCProcessor's convention under NOISE_AT_ZERO by passing 1 - t
  and negating the velocity entering and leaving the processor; track() thus
  always reports in the NOISE_AT_ONE convention
- assign clean prefix tokens the model time at the clean end of the schedule,
  per convention, keeping the existing hard-prefix clamping intact
- add time_grid for wall_x's explicit non-uniform linspace and
  velocity_scale for groot's frozen-prefix velocity weights, rather than
  approximating either

groot and evo1 pick their timestep bucket from a discrete index, not from the
continuous time, so the solver hands them the one it already has via
step_aware rather than making them recover it from time_tensor: on an
accelerator that readback is a device sync on every Euler step. For the same
reason the time_grid path now slices the grid on-device instead of reading
each entry back as a Python float.

evo1, groot and wall_x drop their hand-rolled loops. Each migration is pinned
against a verbatim copy of the loop it replaces.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* chore(wall_x): drop torchdiffeq, now unused after the solver migration

* fix(flow-matching): satisfy mypy in euler_integrate

ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat: add FineART-VLA policy built on pi0.5 (#4184)

* feat(pi052): add language-supervised policy

* fix(pi0_fast): align FAST semantics with OpenPI

Use OpenPI-compatible normalization, token boundaries, balanced loss, and strict full-chunk decoding so training and inference share one sequence contract.

* fix(pi0_fast): apply CI formatting

Keep the parity tests compatible with the repository's current Ruff hooks and remove the requested migration warning from the docs.

* test(pi0_fast): cover shared tokenizer contract

* docs(pi052): shorten configuration descriptions

* refactor(pi052): remove redundant policy code

* refactor(pi052): load native base checkpoint

* feat(pi052): train memory and subtask as one recipe target

* feat(pi052): align scratchpad prompts with one-second history

* fix(pi052): integrate current recipe and interactive runtime contracts

* fix(pi052): decode from the last unmasked prompt token

* Keep PI052 recipe and training extensions policy-local

* Remove obsolete PI052 policy-side rollout planning

* Migrate PI052 checkpoint fields before standard CLI parsing

* fix(pi052): use stable SDPA for joint action attention

* fix(pi05): preserve FP32 arithmetic in joint SDPA

* fix(pi05): use math SDPA for stable low-time gradients

* feat(fineart_vla): rename policy and credit Physical Intelligence pi0.5

* Fix FineART inference compatibility and add opt-in training stabilization

* fix(tests): make FineART-VLA suites honour the optional-dependency tiers

Tier 1 of the fast-tests workflow installs only the base extras, so the seven
modules that reach lerobot.datasets (recipes, eval sampling) failed at import.
Guard those with pytest.importorskip like the rest of the suite, and import the
recipe lazily in the FineART-VLA processor factory (as eo1/wall_x already do) so
the policy modules themselves stay importable without lerobot[dataset].

Also align tests/utils/test_train_utils.py with this branch: eval frames are now
chosen by balanced_eval_indices, not head truncation.

Validation: tier 1 (base+test) 1650 passed / 460 skipped; tier 2 (+dataset) 2981
passed / 429 skipped. pre-commit clean except the 83 mypy diagnostics that clean
main already reports.

* test: trim FineART-VLA PR to the existing forward-parity suites

Drop the policy-specific unit tests added in this PR and revert the extra
cases added to existing test files. The original-vs-LeRobot forward parity
tests remain, along with the fixes existing tests need for the new behavior.

* refactor(fineart_vla): drop legacy pi052 aliases

Remove the pi052 config/processor registry aliases and the pi052
compatibility package, and point the docs at lerobot/fineart_vla_base.

* refactor: keep PI0-FAST and PI0.5 behavior unchanged in the FineART-VLA PR

Move the PI0-FAST openpi alignment and the PI0.5 behavior changes to
codex/pi0fast-openpi-alignment so they can be reviewed and evaluated on
their own:

- pi0_fast: restore main (config, modeling, processor, docs, golden tests).
- pi05: joint-layer FP32 math attention is now opt-in (fp32_joint_attention,
  enabled by FineART-VLA), and the legacy checkpoint loader keeps main's
  behavior. Only subclass hooks with behavior-preserving defaults remain.
- pi_gemma: keep the SDPA helper, drop the process-wide mask dtype cast.

* fix(fineart_vla): flow-only forward, optional kernels, recipe fallbacks

- Accept PI05's prefix_mask/states/state_masks in the flow-only forward and
  delegate RTC/memory training inputs to PI0.5 instead of raising TypeError.
- Guard liger-kernel and kernels with _liger_kernel_available/require_package,
  add fineart_vla and fineart_vla_kernels extras, pin the FlashRT flex-attention
  kernel to v1, and gate the process-wide Liger patch behind use_liger_kernels.
- sample_task() falls back to the canonical task when an episode has no
  task_aug rows.
- Truncate over-long FAST targets with a warning instead of stopping training.
- auto_fit_fast_tokenizer reads the dataset source from dataset_meta.
- Document subtask_joint.yaml as training-only and remove the unused
  encode_prompt_with_targets helper.
- Rename the core model to FineARTVLAPytorch.

* test(fineart_vla): add policy tests; docs, model card and extras

- tests/policies/fineart_vla/test_fineart_vla.py: registration, config and
  processor save/load round-trips, joint-checkpoint rejection, and a CUDA
  forward/predict_action_chunk parity test against PI05Policy with the text,
  FAST and KI paths off.
- Model card template entry, policy README (docs/source/policy_fineart_vla_README.md
  with the usual symlink), citation and license sections in fineart_vla.mdx,
  install instructions for the new extras, and current rollout flags in
  troubleshooting.
- Credit Physical Intelligence in the openpi-derived modeling header.
- Relock with the CI-pinned uv 0.11.30.

* refactor(fineart_vla): remove FlashRT FP8 MLP inference kernels

Drops flashrt_fp8.py, the use_flashrt_fp8_mlp option and its calibration
hook in predict_action_chunk. It was opt-in, inference-only, unused by the
FineART training run, and changed numerics without a task-level check.

* docs(fineart_vla): drop the reported training benchmarks table

* refactor: drop shared-code changes FineART-VLA does not need

Revert to main:
- configs/policies.py: _migrate_pretrained_config hook (and FineART-VLA's
  override). The base checkpoint's configs no longer carry the legacy options.
- datasets/language_render.py: the sample_task() binding.
- scripts/lerobot_train.py: balanced eval subsets and per-group gradient
  clipping; remove datasets/eval_sampling.py and optim/grad_clip.py, plus the
  conditioning/action-expert grad-clip options they served.

None of these were used by the FineART training run.

* refactor(fineart_vla): drop prompt dropout; fold text modules into processor/modeling

- Remove plan/memory/subtask/interjection prompt dropout and its seed; the
  FineART training run left all of them at 0.
- Move the text tokenizer step and message formatting from
  text_processor_fineart_vla.py into processor_fineart_vla.py, and the
  <loc>-tokenizer cache from text_generation.py into modeling_fineart_vla.py.

* refactor: drop the render_messages_processor compatibility step

FineART-VLA pipelines use main's split runtime/training renderers; the base
checkpoint's preprocessor has been updated to match.

* feat(fineart_vla): fit the FAST tokenizer on the training dataset by default

auto_fit_fast_tokenizer now defaults to True and the processor factory reads the
training dataset from dataset_meta or the config's _runtime_dataset_meta (set by
make_policy, as GR00T/LaWAM/MolmoAct2 do). Fine-tuning from a checkpoint
therefore fits a new tokenizer on the new dataset, starting from
action_tokenizer_name. Without a dataset source it warns and uses the base
tokenizer instead of raising.

* fix(fineart_vla): pin kernels below 0.15 in fineart_vla_kernels

kernels>=0.15 makes `import transformers.activations` fail with
"Either a revision or a version must be specified" under the pinned
transformers, so installing the extra broke every transformers-based
policy in the environment. 0.14.1 keeps get_kernel(..., revision=...).

* refactor(fineart_vla): run knowledge insulation through PI0.5's joint layer

FineART-VLA kept its own copy of the PI0.5 joint layer (_compute_layer_ki)
and monkeypatched PaliGemmaWithExpertModel.forward to use it, so fixes to
the PI0.5 layer such as the opt-in FP32 joint attention never reached it.

compute_layer_complete now takes keyword-only knowledge_insulation,
suppress_prefix_grads, attention_fn and norm_backend; the backbone gets a
knowledge_insulation switch and forwards the hooks. With the defaults
PI0.5 runs the same operations (outputs and gradients are bit-identical).
FineART sets the switch and passes FlexAttention/manual attention as
attention_fn and the FlashRT AdaRMS kernels as norm_backend; its copied
layer, forward and monkeypatch are gone. FineART's default KI training
now uses the FP32 joint attention it opts into.

Also move FineART's function-level imports to module level, guarding the
optional liger-kernel, kernels and pyarrow imports.

* fix(fineart_vla): pi05_base loading, config side effects and processor nits

- Load lerobot/pi05_base into FineART-VLA: a FineART-VLA
  _load_as_safetensor override converts OpenPI-format checkpoints (no
  "model." prefix) through PI0.5's conversion, now extracted into
  _convert_openpi_state_dict, and loads them strictly. FineART's state
  dict hook now chains to PI0.5's (keeps MEM's proprio init) and only
  seeds lm_head from the embeddings. Drop the unreachable
  eval_after_pretrained_load / show_openpi_disclaimer hooks; PI0.5's own
  loading matches main again.
- Docs: fine-tune from lerobot/fineart_vla_base with --policy.path so the
  base's FAST layout and recipe are kept, and document starting from
  lerobot/pi05_base.
- use_liger_kernels is opt-in: it patches transformers process-wide.
- recipe_path is cleared once resolved into recipe, so saved checkpoints
  keep their recipe instead of re-reading a file that may change.
- Text and FAST supervision train the VLM: train_expert_only=true with
  either now raises instead of being silently overridden, and the no-op
  _unfreeze_lm_head is gone (unfreeze_lm_head stays as an ignored field
  so existing configs load).
- Use config.text_tokenizer_name instead of hardcoded PaliGemma names.
- Build text-target labels with one vectorized span overlap instead of a
  per-token Python loop.

* test(fineart_vla): pass torch dtypes after the policy dtype unification

main's #4786 made PreTrainedConfig.dtype and PaliGemmaWithExpertModel's
precision real torch.dtype values; the knowledge-insulation backbone
fixture and the FineART/PI0.5 GPU parity test still passed "float32".

* test(fineart_vla): keep one 3B policy on the GPU in the PI0.5 parity test

The CUDA parity test held a PI0.5 and a FineART-VLA policy in fp32 on the
GPU at once (~26 GB), which runs out of memory on the 24 GB L4 GPU-test
runner. The failure kept both models alive through the stored traceback,
so later GPU tests (flux3, lingbot_va, molmoact2, pi0_fast) failed with
CUDA OOM/unknown errors too.

Run PI0.5 first, keep its weights on the CPU, free the GPU, then build
FineART-VLA from the same weights; always release GPU memory on exit.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: refactor(dtype): unify the dtype configuration of policies (#4786)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
refactor(dtype): unify the dtype configuration of policies (#4786)

* feat(configs): make PreTrainedConfig.dtype a real torch.dtype

`dtype` was a bare string that every policy had to convert back into a
`torch.dtype` at its own call site. Nine such converters had drifted apart:
they disagreed on which dtypes they accepted and on what an invalid value
does — `ValueError`, `KeyError`, or a silent fall-through to a different
precision. Nothing in the base class owned the conversion, so each new
policy reinvented it.

Declare the field as `torch.dtype | None` and teach draccus the type once,
through the codecs registered on `PreTrainedConfig`. The on-disk form is
unchanged: `config.json` still stores the plain name `"bfloat16"`, and
`--policy.dtype=bfloat16` still works, so no checkpoint changes shape.
Names resolve against `torch` itself rather than a hardcoded allow-list,
so aliases such as `half` and any dtype a future torch release adds are
supported for free. Strings remain a serialization detail — the Python
API takes the `torch.dtype`.

Per-policy dtype restrictions are kept, with their literals translated;
they encode which precisions a policy was actually validated at, which the
base class cannot know. MolmoAct2's optimizer grouping, for one, still
assumes parameters are either bf16 or not.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: chore(mypy): one ruleset for the whole codebase and mypy 2.3.1 (#4766)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
chore(mypy): one ruleset for the whole codebase and mypy 2.3.1 (#4766)

* chore(mypy): collapse per-module overrides into one ruleset

Every module except lerobot.rl now passes the gate, so the 25 per-module override blocks are replaced by a single [tool.mypy] ruleset for all checked code. The only exceptions are lerobot.rl (not typed yet) and the vendored molmoact2_hf_model. The package root (__init__, __version__) is now checked too and already passes.

The disallow_untyped_defs / disallow_incomplete_defs / check_untyped_defs flags that only five modules carried are dropped; stricter settings will be adopted repo-wide instead of per module. The obsolete "enable mypy gradually" TODO is removed and the AGENTS.md mypy note is updated.

* chore(mypy): enable the strictness checks that already pass everywhere

warn_redundant_casts, extra_checks and strict_bytes (the mypy 2.x default) plus the deprecated, exhaustive-match, redundant-self, truthy-iterable and unused-awaitable error codes report nothing on the current code, so they are adopted repo-wide at no cost and guard new code from now on.

* chore(mypy): run the pre-commit hook on the whole tree

The hook passed only the staged files, and with follow_imports = skip every other module became Any, so local commits reported about 43 errors that CI (--all-files) never sees, e.g. "Cannot determine type of calibration" on a robot file checked without robot.py. The hook now sets pass_filenames: false and [tool.mypy] lists the checked paths, so a clean checkout analyses the same 557 files locally and in CI. exclude_gitignore keeps ignored scratch files out; untracked files under those paths are still checked.

The hook's files pattern mirrors that list and includes pyproject.toml, so config-only changes run it too. The generated gRPC modules (_pb2.py, _pb2_grpc.py) are excluded, as they already are from ruff. The stale "Uncomment when ready to use" TODO above the hook is removed, and AGENTS.md now says what the gate checks and how to run it.

* chore(mypy): enable strict_equality

strict_equality reports comparisons that can never be true. Its only hit was LiberoProcessorStep.transform_features, which compared PipelineFeatureType keys against FeatureType.STATE: the filter never matched, a stray FeatureType.STATE key was added and the observation group never got observation.state. It now rebuilds the observation group around the flattened 8-dim state, like the xvla LiberoProcessorStep. Nothing in src calls this method today; a test pins the corrected output.

* chore(mypy): enable local_partial_types

local_partial_types stops mypy from inferring a module-level None variable's type from uses in other scopes; mypy 2.x enables it by default. Its only hit was wall_x PRIORITY_ORDER, now annotated as the OrderedDict | None that get_task_instruction accepts.

* chore(mypy): enable the truthy-bool error code

truthy-bool reports objects used in a boolean context although they are always truthy (no __bool__/__len__), which is how an `if obj:` meant as a None check silently passes. Both hits were dead checks: create_camera_instance tested `if instance:` after every branch had assigned a camera (its trailing return was unreachable), and the rollout teleop log line re-checked cfg.teleop inside an `is not None` block.

* chore(mypy): disable implicit re-exports

With implicit_reexport = false a name is only importable from a module that defines it or lists it in __all__, which enforces canonical imports. Six importers reached a name through a module that merely imported it and now import it from where it is defined (lerobot_types, utils.import_utils, utils.io_utils, fastwam wan.model, bi_so_leader's config module).

wall_x.qwen_model drops the transformers Qwen2_5_VLVisionConfig from its imports and __all__. Its config module never re-exported the class and nothing imports it from there, but it was a declared public name: import it from transformers instead.

* chore(mypy): warn about unused type: ignore comments

warn_unused_ignores reports suppressions that no longer suppress anything, so stale ignores cannot pile up or hide a later real error on the same line. It flagged 36, 32 of them already stale on main:
- 18 import-line ignores (incl. the camera 'TODO: add type stubs' ones) made redundant by ignore_missing_imports; the two after a noqa on the VLABench imports, which mypy never parsed, go too;
- 3 protobuf attr-defined ignores, redundant now that the generated _pb2 modules are excluded;
- 8 for error codes the ruleset does not enable: no-untyped-def (reader.frames_df gets a return annotation), type-arg (the *_delta_indices properties return list[int]) and no-any-return;
- 7 on expressions or class lines whose operand is Any in the gate (the push_to_hub shadowing keeps its rename TODO).

The six yaml/requests import ignores move to a per-module ignore_missing_imports override: mypy 1.19.1 needs it and mypy 2.x accepts it, so bumping the pinned mypy will not report them as unused.

* chore(mypy): require error codes on type: ignore comments

The ignore-without-code error code rejects a bare `# type: ignore`, which silences every error on its line instead of the one intended. After the unused-ignore cleanup a single bare ignore remained, on spec.loader in the hub env loader; spec.loader is None is now part of the existing ImportError guard, so the ignore is gone. spec_from_file_location always sets a loader when it returns a spec, so behaviour is unchanged.

* chore(mypy): list the next strictness candidates in the ruleset

warn_unreachable, strict_equality_for_none and check_untyped_defs are worth enabling next but each needs a fix PR first; the ruleset now records them with their current error counts and the caveat that matters for each.

* chore(mypy): bump mypy to 2.3.1

pre-commit ran mypy 1.19.1 while the dev extra (mypy>=1.19.1) already resolved to 2.3.1, so `pre-commit` and `uv run mypy` could disagree. The hook now pins mirrors-mypy v2.3.1 and the dev extra allows the whole 2.x line (>=2.0.0,<3.0.0); the lockfile keeps 2.3.1.

2.3.1 reports two errors that 1.19.1 missed, both fixed without changing behaviour:
- OpenCVCamera._validate_fourcc unpacked the Optional config.fourcc; it now binds it locally and raises if it is None (both callers already check it).
- DatasetReader's column-view cache compared hf_dataset against an Optional attribute with `is not`, which newer mypy uses to re-widen hf_dataset; the comparison now goes through a local.

mypy 2.x no longer reports yaml/requests as untyped under the global ignore_missing_imports, so their override is dropped, and the warn_unreachable candidate count is updated to what 2.3.1 reports (40).
